title: First Chapter Improvement: Hooking Readers Through Oriented Emotion

anti_hallucination_instructions.real_world_facts: Clearly separate real-world facts from fictional world-building. Do not invent factual information.
anti_hallucination_instructions.fictional_world_building: You may expand or fictionalize freely in made-up settings as long as it is internally consistent.
anti_hallucination_instructions.fallback_strategy: When unsure about a fact, do not guess. Flag the unknown and suggest additional research or clearly label the content as fictionalized.
anti_hallucination_instructions.consistent_output_format: At the beginning of the output, include a brief note explaining how facts were treated and whether anything was flagged for review or fictionalized.

fact_handling_strategy: Avoid hallucinations by flagging uncertainties. Recommend research rather than fabricate. Distinguish between real-world accuracy and fictional consistency.

placeholder_convention.commentary_instruction: If placeholders are used, briefly explain the decision in a preface note.

source_guidance.fallback_label: If a source cannot be verified, label the fact as 'assumed' or recommend external validation.

fiction_consistency_rules.fictional_consistency_priority: If real-world facts contradict established fictional logic, prioritize internal consistency unless instructed otherwise.

description: Analyze the first chapter of a novel to identify and resolve five common failures that often cause readers to disengage early. Your goal is to help the author create a gripping opening that hooks the reader through oriented emotion—anchoring the speculative or unfamiliar within a named protagonist's emotional context.

scoring_criteria.90-100: Exceptional opening that masterfully employs all best practices. Ready for submission.
scoring_criteria.80-89: Strong opening with minor adjustments needed. Close to publication quality.
scoring_criteria.70-79: Good foundation with several areas for improvement. Solid but needs refinement.
scoring_criteria.60-69: Average opening with significant issues that prevent reader engagement.
scoring_criteria.50-59: Below average with major structural problems requiring substantial revision.
scoring_criteria.40-49: Poor opening with fundamental flaws in multiple areas.
scoring_criteria.30-39: Severely flawed opening that fails to meet basic genre expectations.
scoring_criteria.20-29: Major reconstruction needed. Current version unlikely to retain readers.
scoring_criteria.10-19: Critical failure across all metrics. Complete rewrite recommended.
scoring_criteria.1-9: Unworkable opening that fundamentally misunderstands storytelling principles.

scoring_factors: Genre alignment and reader expectations (20 points)
Prose quality and voice consistency (15 points)

science_fiction.reader_expectations: Technological wonder balanced with human stakes, scientific plausibility, future implications
science_fiction.common_pitfalls: Tech-dump exposition, protagonist passive to technology, unclear relationship between science and conflict
science_fiction.opening_priorities: Ground speculative elements in character need, establish the 'what if' through personal stakes

fantasy.reader_expectations: Magical systems with clear rules, rich world-building, archetypal conflicts with fresh twists
fantasy.common_pitfalls: Magic system exposition, generic medieval settings, prophecy/chosen one clichés
fantasy.opening_priorities: Show magic through character interaction, establish world's unique rules via conflict

literary_fiction.reader_expectations: Psychological depth, nuanced prose, character-driven conflict, thematic resonance
literary_fiction.common_pitfalls: Navel-gazing without plot momentum, overly subtle stakes, pretentious voice
literary_fiction.opening_priorities: Establish character's internal conflict, hint at broader themes through specific details

mystery_thriller.reader_expectations: Immediate intrigue, competent protagonist, logical plot progression, satisfying resolution setup
mystery_thriller.common_pitfalls: Withholding information artificially, passive protagonist, red herrings without foundation
mystery_thriller.opening_priorities: Establish the puzzle/threat, show protagonist's capability, create reader investment in solution

romance.reader_expectations: Emotional connection, sexual tension, relationship obstacles, satisfying romantic arc setup
romance.common_pitfalls: Instalove without foundation, contrived obstacles, stereotypical character dynamics
romance.opening_priorities: Establish protagonist's emotional wound/need, hint at romantic conflict, show character appeal

horror.reader_expectations: Atmosphere of dread, escalating tension, relatable fears, visceral impact
horror.common_pitfalls: Gore without emotional investment, jump scares without buildup, unclear threat parameters
horror.opening_priorities: Establish normal world before disruption, ground fear in character vulnerability

young_adult.reader_expectations: Relatable teenage concerns, age-appropriate stakes, authentic voice, coming-of-age themes
young_adult.common_pitfalls: Adults writing 'down' to teens, outdated slang, dismissing teen concerns as trivial
young_adult.opening_priorities: Authentic teenage voice, stakes that matter to character's development, immediate relatability

historical_fiction.reader_expectations: Period authenticity, historical integration, universal themes through specific context
historical_fiction.common_pitfalls: Info-dumping historical context, anachronistic language/attitudes, history overshadowing character
historical_fiction.opening_priorities: Show period through character's daily reality, establish historical stakes with personal impact

diagnostics.problem: The reader has no focal point for empathy or prediction.
diagnostics.basic_fix: Ensure the POV character is named in the first natural sentence. No biography—just clarity.

high_priority: Name the protagonist within the first 2-3 sentences maximum
Establish clear POV perspective (first, third limited, etc.) immediately
Ground the reader in whose head they're experiencing the story
medium_priority: Reveal protagonist's role/occupation through action rather than exposition
Show character's personality through their reaction to opening situation
Establish character's approximate age/life stage through context clues
low_priority: Hint at character's background through specific details
Use character's name naturally in dialogue or action
Establish character's relationships to other people mentioned

diagnostics.problem: Description without desire, fear, or consequence fails to activate interest.
diagnostics.basic_fix: Pair any world or action detail with a felt want, dread, or risk of loss.

high_priority: Establish what the character wants/needs in the immediate scene
Show what happens if the character fails to achieve their goal
Create time pressure or urgency around the character's objective
medium_priority: Connect immediate scene stakes to larger story consequences
Show character's emotional investment in the outcome
Establish obstacles that make success uncertain
low_priority: Layer in hints of future complications
Show how current situation affects character's long-term goals
Add secondary characters whose needs conflict with protagonist's

diagnostics.problem: Cognitive overload stalls immersion when abstract lore isn't grounded in need.
diagnostics.basic_fix: Introduce one coined term at a time via the protagonist's direct experience or problem.

high_priority: Introduce maximum one new term per paragraph
Show invented concepts through character action, not explanation
Make each new term immediately relevant to character's current problem
medium_priority: Use familiar context clues to help readers understand new terms
Have character react emotionally to invented elements
Establish clear cause-and-effect relationships with new concepts
low_priority: Create consistent naming patterns for invented terms
Use character dialogue to naturally define new concepts
Build complexity gradually rather than front-loading information

diagnostics.issue: Opening with Setting or Lore, Not Character
diagnostics.problem: Detached exposition lacks emotional relevance or neural engagement.
diagnostics.basic_fix: Recast setting details through the character's current problem or choice.

high_priority: Start with character in motion (physical or emotional)
Filter all setting details through character's immediate needs/concerns
Show how environment affects character's ability to achieve their goal
medium_priority: Use character's expertise/ignorance to naturally reveal world details
Show character's relationship to their environment (comfort, fear, familiarity)
Reveal setting through character's sensory experience and reactions
low_priority: Layer in historical/cultural context through character's assumptions
Use environmental details to reflect character's emotional state
Show how setting creates or solves problems for the character

diagnostics.problem: Prologues, dreams, or tone shifts violate reader expectations and trust.
diagnostics.basic_fix: Start in the dominant POV, voice, and genre mode of the main story.

high_priority: Eliminate prologues unless absolutely essential to plot comprehension
Avoid dream sequences, flashbacks, or 'it was all a story' openings
Match opening tone and style to the genre promise on the book cover
medium_priority: Establish consistent narrative voice from the first sentence
Ensure opening chapter represents the typical reading experience
Begin with the protagonist who will carry the majority of the story
low_priority: Use genre-appropriate pacing and scene structure
Incorporate expected genre elements (magic, technology, romance, etc.) early
Avoid misleading readers about the type of story they're beginning

instructions: Begin by providing a numerical score (1-100) with brief justification based on the scoring criteria.
Identify which of the 5 common failures (if any) are present.
For each identified issue, provide specific fixes organized by priority level (High/Medium/Low).
Consider the genre-specific expectations and adjust recommendations accordingly.

Focus your suggestions on:
  - The first 1–2 paragraphs.
  - The clarity of protagonist, stakes, and emotional orientation.
  - The genre alignment and promise of tone.
Ensure the rewritten or improved suggestions match the genre and intended audience.
Conclude with a short paragraph summarizing how your recommendations increase reader engagement.
Be honest and incisive with your feedback. Avoid social niceties and target as deep and honest evaluation as possible.

output_format.section_3: PRIORITY FIXES: [Organized by High/Medium/Low priority for each issue]
output_format.section_5: ENGAGEMENT IMPACT: [Summary of how fixes improve reader retention]

optional_follow_up: If the user would like, offer a rewritten or revised version of the opening paragraph(s) using their existing material, implementing the improvements.
